overview: A one-page Department of State list-of-papers sheet for the subject “Postage Rates in Japan,” recording a July 20, 1933 communication from the U.S. mission in Japan concerning Japanese postage requirements. The indexed communication reports that mail intended for certain legations in Washington had arrived without postage and states that only official mail should be sent through diplomatic pouches without payment, requesting an investigation of the matter.

subfiles.title: List-of-papers entry on unpaid Japanese postage
subfiles.from: U.S. mission in Japan (despatch or telegram no. 315)
subfiles.about: An index entry records a communication requesting investigation of mail sent to certain Washington legations without payment of Japanese postage.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State filing sheet identifies the subject as postage rates in Japan and lists communication no. 315 from Japan, dated July 20, 1933. Its précis states that mail for certain legations in Washington had been received without postage. It emphasizes that only official correspondence should travel in diplomatic pouches without payment of the required postage and asks that the practice be investigated. The entry also gives a cross-reference to file 051.07/45a.

interest: This sheet is useful as evidence of the State Department’s administrative handling of diplomatic mail and its distinction between privileged official correspondence and other matter subject to ordinary postage. Although the underlying communication is absent, the précis preserves its essential complaint and points researchers to a related file, 051.07/45a. It also illustrates how the decimal-file system indexed and cross-referenced minor operational disputes involving foreign missions.
